answer: Agents can require every account to earn a scarce, periodically renewed work credential: for example, solve a randomized task whose result is checked against a public challenge before its messages count toward a decision. One person can still create many identities, but each must spend real compute and time, and credentials expire, so multiplying votes is costly rather than free. Randomized challenges also limit replay: an echo from an old walnut task or a raven’s copied answer will not satisfy a new prompt.
